insert.name: insert
insert.description: Memory management skill for capturing durable facts from text chunks, enhanced with entity preservation, temporal anchor retention, and pre-storage validation to prevent data loss during compression.
insert.instruction_template:
Skill: Insert New Memory with Entity Preservation
Purpose: Capture new, durable facts from the current text chunk that are missing in memory. Enforce strict retention of named entities, dates, and direct answers to prevent information loss.
When to use:
- The text chunk introduces new facts, events, plans, or context worth storing.
- The information is stable and likely useful later.
How to apply:
1. Entity & Temporal Extraction: Scan the text to identify all Named Entities (people, locations, organizations), Dates, Times, Durations, and Direct Answers.
2. Entity-Aware Compression: Synthesize the memory. CRITICAL: You must retain the extracted Entity names, exact Dates, and specific values. Do not summarize "Stadio Nacional" as "a venue" or "May 5th" as "later that day". Preserve fidelity to key identifiers.
3. Pre-Storage Validation: Review the drafted memory against the original text. Check: Are all critical entities present? Is the temporal anchor exact? If any critical detail is dropped, revise the draft immediately.
4. Duplicate Check: Compare the validated memory against retrieved items to avoid duplicates.
Constraints:
- Skip trivial, fleeting, or speculative content.
- NEVER omit specific names, numbers, or dates that were explicitly stated.
- Do not update or delete existing memories.
- Action type must be INSERT only.
Output Format:
ACTION: INSERT
MEMORY_ITEM: <content adhering to entity preservation rules>
REASONING: <explanation citing retained entities and dates>

update.name: update
update.description: Memory management skill for revising an existing memory item when the text chunk provides corrections or new details.
update.instruction_template:
Skill: Update Existing Memory
Purpose: Revise a retrieved memory with new or corrected information from the text chunk.
When to use:
- The text chunk clarifies, corrects, or extends a retrieved memory.
How to apply:
- Select the best matching memory item.
- Merge new details into a single updated item.
- Preserve accurate details that still hold.
Constraints:
- Do not create new memories.
- Do not delete items.
Action type: UPDATE only.

delete.name: delete
delete.description: Memory management skill for removing memory items that are incorrect, outdated, or superseded.
delete.instruction_template:
Skill: Delete Invalid Memory
Purpose: Remove a retrieved memory that is wrong, outdated, or superseded by the text chunk.
When to use:
- The text chunk clearly contradicts a memory.
- A plan or fact is explicitly canceled or replaced.
How to apply:
- Only delete when evidence is explicit.
Constraints:
- If uncertain, prefer no action over deletion.
Action type: DELETE only.

noop.name: noop
noop.description: Memory management skill for confirming that no memory changes are required.
noop.instruction_template:
Skill: No Operation
Purpose: Confirm no memory changes are needed for the text chunk.
When to use:
- The text chunk contains no new, corrective, or actionable information.
Constraints:
- Emit NOOP only if none of the selected skills produce actions.
Action type: NOOP only.
